2.text: Perhaps it will not be out of place to mention here another Chukchee

3.text: legend which seems to be even more ancient. In olden times there lived in

4.text: the Anui Mountains a large beast called Keliˊlhu.¹ He was tall and long,

5.text: had a huge mouth which opened wide, and long-clawed paws. A certain

6.text: young herdsman wandered among the crags, looking for a lost reindeer, and

7.text: was seen and eaten by Keliˊlhu.

8.text: Some time afterward the young man’s father started to look for him.

9.text: He went among the crags, and soon met Keliˊlhu. He said, “Keliˊlhu, have

10.text: a laugh! I am fat, you will eat me; my reindeer are fatter, you will eat

11.text: them too.” — “Ha, ha, ha!” laughed Keliˊlhu; and his mouth opened so

12.text: wide that his upper jaw reached his back, while his lower jaw hung down to

13.text: his breast. When he stopped laughing, he closed his jaws with his paws,

14.text: and continued his pursuit; but the man had succeeded in gaining ground.

15.text: After a while the beast approached him again; but the man repeated, “Keliˊlhu,

16.text: have a laugh! I am fat, you will eat me; my reindeer are fatter, you will

17.text: eat them too.” — “Ha, ha, ha!” laughed Keliˊlhu; and his jaws sprang as

18.text: wide apart as before, and he closed them in the same manner, and continued

19.text: his pursuit. At last they reached the village, where a number of young men

20.text: killed Keliˊlhu with spears; but he had also killed many, because he was light

21.text: and nimble, jumped high, bit with his teeth, and smote with his paws.

22.text: PRESENT HABITAT. — The villages of the Maritime Chukchee are situated

23.text: on the Arctic coast between Cape Erri and East Cape, and on the coast of

24.text: Bering Sea between East Cape and Anadyr Bay, except where a few Eskimo

25.text: settlements are interspersed, — two near East Cape, and seven between Indian

26.text: Point and Cape Ulakhpen (Улахпенъ). The latter is called by the natives

27.text: Wuteˊen, the same name as the village close by.

28.text: The Reindeer camps are scattered over the whole country to the northeast

29.text: of a line drawn from the mouth of the Indighirka River to Cape Anannon.

30.text: The part of the country lying to the west of the rivers Chaun and Anadyr

31.text: forms the so-called “Chukchee territory”² (Чукотская землица). This territory,

32.text: according to the obsolete but not yet abolished paragraph of the Russian

33.text: Code, is considered to be “not thoroughly subdued.” Its inhabitants, as well

34.text: as all other Chukchee, have the privilege of settling all their affairs according

35.text: to their own customs, including even murder if committed within the limits

36.text: of their own territories. Such privileges sometimes lead to strange results.

37.text: G. Dyachkoff³ relates the following incident, that occurred among the

38.text: Olutora Koryak. In 1882 a man was murdered. The brothers of the murdered

39.text: man refrained from the usual revenge, and sent a complaint to the magistrate
